title: Cuprous
textbookText: Most of the transition metals have variable valency. They can form more than one cation. Classically, while naming these ions, ‘ous’ suffix is used for relatively lower valency state and ‘ic’ suffix is used for relatively higher valency state. Nowadays, the charge on the metal ion follows the name of the metal in Roman numerals. This is referred to as the Stock method. For example, the names of the iron ions are Iron (II) and Iron (III) and the names of the copper ions are Copper (I) and Copper (II). Some of the metal ions with variable valency is given below
